transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Ravi Menon (Aperture Head of ML), Claire DuPont (Aperture Security Lead), Marco Silva (Aperture Platform)

[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and we'll jump in. I'm Samantha, I'm the AE on this account. Daniel's our SE who'll cover the technical bits.
[00:12] Ravi Menon: Hey all, Ravi here. We run a real-time recommendations pipeline and looking at LLM inference for several internal tools. Security is the gating factor for us.
[00:22] Claire DuPont: Claire, security. We need to map Redwood into our compliance matrix — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, you know the usual.
[00:30] Daniel Cho: Great, thanks Claire. We'll go through high-level posture then dive into specific integration points — SAML/SSO, key management, audit logs, retention and deployment options.
[00:42] Marco Silva: We also want to know differences between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Cost/latency tradeoffs and what we can control.

Summary: Early stage — Aperture is comfortable with cloud providers but requires SOC2 proof, wants BYOK or HSM option, long audit retention, SIEM export, and strict RBAC. They prefer EU data residency for some workloads.

[02:10] Daniel Cho: On compliance — Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is working on ISO 27001. We can share the attestations and the summary. For outbound artifacts we provide a SOC2 summary and a controls matrix.
[02:25] Claire DuPont: When you say 'share attestations' can you also provide scope? e.g. is hosted API in-scope, what about private deployments? We need the scoping to match our vendor risk assessment.
[02:35] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, we'll include the scope. Hosted API is in-scope for our SOC2; Dedicated and Private have different scopes — Private will typically be customer managed control plane and we'll provide docs for that model. We'll attach a matrix.

[05:00] Marco Silva: KMS — we want to keep control of keys. BYOK or HSM integration is non-negotiable for certain datasets. How do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:12] Daniel Cho: We support BYOK via cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations for Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption where the customer key wraps the service key. For Dedicated we can enable customer-owned KMS in a VPC-backed configuration. There's also an option for customers to manage keys in an HSM in their VPC and we integrate via our key-broker.
[05:40] Ravi Menon: So for Hosted, if the key is in our AWS KMS, are tokens or raw text ever visible to Redwood keyspace? We need explicit guarantee that plaintext never leaves our control.
[05:52] Daniel Cho: Good question. For hosted envelope mode, plaintext is decrypted in the runtime — so we understand why you'd be cautious. If the requirement is absolute zero plaintext exposure to Redwood-managed service, we recommend Private deployment where you control the runtime and keys. Dedicated with customer-managed KMS is the middle ground — we still host the runtime but keys never leave your KMS.

[07:30] Claire DuPont: Audit logs: retention, export and integration with our Splunk stack. How granular are the logs? Is token-level logging available? Can we export to S3?
[07:45] Daniel Cho: Audit logs include per-request metadata: timestamp, model, route, user-id (if sent), and a trace id. We also emit higher-level cost traces and latency breakdowns. We currently have export to S3 and direct webhook pushes to SIEMs; Splunk integration is common via S3 or HTTP ingest. Token-level logs (full tokens) are sensitive — by default we do not store full request payloads unless customers opt into longer retention for debugging, but we can configure redaction.
[08:20] Ravi Menon: For eDiscovery we need 7 years retention on certain logs and immutable storage options for audit trails. Is that supported?
[08:30] Daniel Cho: We can support long retention via export to customer S3 with lifecycle policies — effectively make it immutable with S3 Object Lock. For Hosted short-term logs are retained for our operational needs; for long-term retention we recommend automated export. Private deployments obviously you can set your own retention.

[10:05] Claire DuPont: Identity: SSO and SCIM for provisioning, we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM. How mature is your SSO?
[10:15] Samantha Ortiz: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC supports roles: admin, developer, viewer, and token-scoped roles. For Dedicated/Private we can sync with customer IdP and map groups to roles.
[10:32] Marco Silva: Do you support session timeout and step-up authentication?
[10:36] Daniel Cho: Session timeout is configurable on the console; step-up (MFA enforced via IdP) is supported since it's enforced at the IdP side.

[12:00] Ravi Menon: On RBAC, we need fine-grained gating: ability to restrict model deploys, rollouts, and cost controls per team. Also ability to restrict export of logs to certain roles.
[12:15] Daniel Cho: That's part of our RBAC model — role bindings per route/model and per-environment. You can set which roles can start rollouts, approve canary, etc. Audit logs record the actor. We should make sure our role names map to your internal ones; we'll share a mapping doc.

[14:40] Claire DuPont: Network controls — VPC peering, private endpoints, no public egress for inference traffic. Do you support private networking?
[14:52] Daniel Cho: Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports VPC-only communication. For Hosted API there's a private link option for certain clouds, otherwise public endpoints. If you need zero-public egress, Private is the path.

[16:20] Marco Silva: Performance: if we go Dedicated with our own KMS, what does failover look like? If KMS in our account has outage, does Redwood have fallback keys? That would violate our key control.
[16:33] Daniel Cho: We don't do automatic fallback to Redwood-managed keys if you've configured customer-managed KMS. If your KMS is unavailable, the runtime will fail calls — we can design retry/backoff or fallback policies but not to compromise key ownership. We can also set secondary key replicas in multiple regions in your KMS.

[18:50] Samantha Ortiz: On penetration testing and vulnerability management — we can share our last pentest summary and have a process for MRA (mutual risk assessment). For Private deployments, customers often run their own pen tests.
[19:05] Claire DuPont: We will require a pen test attestation and timeline for remediations on medium/high findings. Also a documented patch cadence.
[19:15] Daniel Cho: Noted — we'll include our patch cadence doc and the last three months of CVE management summary.

[21:40] Ravi Menon: Data residency — some inference workloads must remain in EU. Can we pin models to a region?
[21:50] Daniel Cho: Yes, routing policies let you pin by region and model. Hosted has region options; Dedicated and Private give you stronger controls. We'll note which models are available in which region as part of our model catalog.

[23:00] Marco Silva: Logging overhead/per-token cost — if we enable token-level traces for debugging, what's the performance impact?
[23:12] Daniel Cho: There's a performance and cost tradeoff. Token-level traces increase storage and some latency; we can enable sampling or prefix caching to reduce impact. Also Redwood Optimize suggests batching/kv-cache tweaks — sorry, I said KV cash earlier — code for the KV cache that holds context.

[25:00] Ravi Menon: Can we demo with our sample payloads? We want to ensure latency SLOs for our 150ms target on summary generation.
[25:10] Samantha Ortiz: Yes — next step is an SE-led benchmarking session. Daniel will run a live test with your sample payloads on Dedicated and Hosted to compare.

[27:40] Claire DuPont: Legal: Data processing agreement, DPA, and subprocessor list — we need to review before pilot.
[27:50] Samantha Ortiz: We'll send the latest DPA and our subprocessors list. For Private deployments subprocessor exposure is minimal since you're self-hosting.

[30:10] Marco Silva: What about rate limiting and quotas? Our workload is spiky. We need burst capacity and predictable throughput.
[30:20] Daniel Cho: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and burst capacity options. We also have autoscaling policies. For Hosted, quotas are enforced at the tenant level. We can show sample configs.

[32:00] Ravi Menon: Regarding retention policy enforcement, we want a simple UI to set retention per route and automatic exports to our S3 with Object Lock for immutability. Is that plumbed today?
[32:14] Daniel Cho: There's console support for per-route retention settings and an export pipeline to S3. Object Lock depends on your S3 settings. For Hosted we'll help configure the export. For Private, you control the export side.

[34:00] Claire DuPont: Incident response: will Redwood notify us of security events affecting our data? SLA for notifications?
[34:12] Samantha Ortiz: We have incident response SLAs for customers with enterprise contracts. We issue notifications based on severity and provide a timeline and remediation plan. We'll share a template incident playbook.

[36:20] Marco Silva: A nitty gritty — where do model weights live in each deployment mode? If someone spins up a model in Hosted, are weights stored on Redwood infra that could be accessed? We need control around model assets.
[36:35] Daniel Cho: For Hosted, weights are stored on Redwood-managed storage; access controls are internal and audited. For Dedicated we can provide tenant-isolated storage and for Private you host weights inside your environment. We'll document our access controls and encryption-in-rest for model artifacts.

[38:00] Ravi Menon: Can we limit who can pull logs that contain PII? We need role-based restrictions and possibly log redaction.
[38:10] Daniel Cho: Yes — RBAC combined with redaction policies can block full payload visibility. We redacted sensitive fields by default and can provide tokenization hooks so PII never lands in logs.

[40:20] Claire DuPont: A couple of quick asks: 1) Provide sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping examples; 2) Provide a sample audit log export with dummy entries; 3) Provide the SOC2 scope doc.
[40:35] Samantha Ortiz: We'll send those three items.

[42:00] Daniel Cho: Pilot recommendation: start with Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with customer-managed KMS and SAML SSO. Run a 2-week bench with sample payloads, capture telemetry and audit logs exported to your S3. If governance needs tighten, we can move to Private.

[43:10] Ravi Menon: Sounds reasonable. For cost — will you provide an estimate for the Dedicated pilot?
[43:18] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, I'll share a pilot quote and a cost model for expected token/throughput and burst.

[44:40] Claire DuPont: Recap and decisions: Aperture wants SOC2 + ISO artifacts, DPA and subprocessor list, sample SAML/SCIM, KMS/HSM runbook, and an SE benchmark session. Pilot will be Dedicated in EU with BYOK.

[45:05] Samantha Ortiz: Great — we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the SE deep-dive. Any final questions?
[45:12] Marco Silva: Nothing else from me. Thanks.
[45:18] Ravi Menon: Thanks everyone.
[45:22] Claire DuPont: Thanks.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: some words mis-transcribed ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache", occasional dropped words). Natural speech present: interruptions, filler words, and brief crosstalk.

References shared: SOC2_summary.pdf (link), DPA_v3.pdf (link), SAML_SCIM_examples.zip (link), VPC_private-deploy-runbook.md (link), pilot-quote-Aperture.xlsx (link).
questions: Does Redwood provide SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts?
How is BYOK/HSM supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
Can audit logs be exported to customer S3 with Object Lock for immutability?
What RBAC granularity is available for restricting log access and rollout controls?
